name: 45757-mixedprompt-1b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1), plus 1 GiB of pinned host DRAM reserved as a KV tier. No disk, no remote store, no NIC on the serving path.
architecture: LlamaForCausalLM, bf16, 1.24B parameters -- the ungated mirror of the gated meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=16, bound at 200 requests, warmup 10% and cooldown 10%, static seed 45757.
workload: Mixed-length prompts, long answers, single turn, no reuse. guidellm `synthetic_text`: prompt_tokens 34816 drawn over [4096, 65536], output_tokens 1024 fixed (min=max), temperature 0, 200 requests -- about 7.0M prompt tokens and 205K generated tokens end to end.
purpose: A long-document analysis assistant on one GPU, serving 16 concurrent users book-length prompts with full-page answers.
launch:
# ENGINE: vLLM at commit 731fb3323d5c42f0a6fe2843084b782a7f7bf035 (v0.23.1rc0-143-g731fb3323d5c),
# one H100 80GB HBM3 of an a3 node, driven in-process by guidellm's `vllm_python` backend.

model: unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct
tensor-parallel-size: 1
max-model-len: 73728

# Sized to the workload's LONGEST prompt (65536), not to a scheduling convenience: this
# deployment is meant to admit a prompt in one step rather than in eight. Legal because
# max-model-len is 73728. HAZARD: lowering it does not fail, it quietly moves the engine to a
# different operating point at rc=0.
max-num-batched-tokens: 65536
block-size: 16

# KEEP ON ONE LINE AS JSON: the config reader is flat, so a dict written as an indented YAML block
# is silently dropped and never reaches AsyncEngineArgs -- the engine would then start with no
# offload tier at all, at rc=0.
kv-transfer-config: {"kv_connector": "OffloadingConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_connector_extra_config": {"cpu_bytes_to_use": 1073741824}}

async-scheduling: false
